title: After Robichaux: Piron again and having no band of his own
summary: He went back to Piron in 1928 and says he never led a band under his own name.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: It was Red Happy. I'll tell you what I was going to ask you. Again, going back to Cartrell, we always seem to be getting back to him, but, uh, I hear that he would go into Philip Werlein's and test the drums.
They could let you know of your...
Uh, getting back to your story, where did you go after Robichaud? Do you remember where you went after that?

Yeah. That was during the time when, uh, when Paul Bobberin, we left P-Rong Band to go with a kid, uh, Sonny Allen. Uh-huh. I mean, with, uh, Sonny Allen and them and Walter P. Sean, that's where I went, P-Rong Band. All that was in 1928. And I worked in that band a good while.
That was after you made that recording, was it? Yeah, it was way after.
Oh, yeah. It was way after.
Did you ever, uh, I hear you had a band of your own called the Sonny South Band, was that
right? No, that was my band of my own. Was it? No, not me. I never played in that band even. I got a friend of the one. That was running by Sydney Keaton in the Sonny South. Yeah. I knew it.
Did you ever have a band of your own under your own name?

No, I used to take little spot jobs, you know, but I never, I could have made bands lots of times on my own name, but I just, I used to take little small jobs on my own like that. We just, we'd give it no title, you know. I used to take a big baritone sax. Yeah.
